name: Fairmont Century Plaza
positioning: Fairmont Century Plaza, a mid-century hotel in Century City designed by architect Minoru Yamasaki
best_for: Travelers who want a central Los Angeles base and will have a car
Guests interested in a spa with biohacking treatments
Guests drawn to Hollywood and music history

facts.text: The mid-century design is by architect Minoru Yamasaki.
A push for landmark status that began in 2009 saved the curving main building from demolition.
The spa has a salt room, a blue-light rain bath and a steam room.
The workout center is equipped with Technogym machines and has a guided Theragun recovery center.
The hotel has a rooftop pool.
The Fairmont 1 King room has floor-to-ceiling windows, a private balcony with outdoor seating and Le Labo bath amenities.
Fairmont Gold rooms and suites include access to the Fairmont Gold Lounge with breakfast, canapes and private arrival.
Rooms look either west toward the ocean or east toward downtown.
The hotel is a short drive from Beverly Hills, Culver City and Westwood.
The hotel has a resident canine ambassador, a black lab.

highlights.text: The elevators are named after Sonny & Cher, who performed nightly at the hotel in the 1970s.
The spa's biohacking offering includes an antigravity bed in an infrared sauna, Normatec lymphatic drainage pants and a red light mask.
The Directors 1 Bedroom Suite has views toward the Pacific Ocean, three balconies and a kitchenette.
The hotel has hosted the Emmys, the Grammys and the first State Dinner held outside the White House.

considerations.text: A car is recommended, with easy access to the 10 and the 405.
Century City is not the main attraction; the appeal is the short commute to everywhere else.
A subway stop under construction next to the hotel is due to open in 2027, with a connection to Santa Monica and LAX.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Fairmont Century Plaza Los Angeles at Beverly Hills
